currentState.summary: SignalRClient negotiates once and hands a reduced ConnectionData to a target-specific communication client. Native Tokio keeps shared action storage and implements retry policies, but reconnects directly to the old negotiated WebSocket endpoint and repeats the handshake. WASM polls every 100 ms, logs disconnected/error status, never applies ReconnectionConfig or DisconnectionHandler, exposes an empty ReconnectionHandler, and is not linked to a real browser test suite. MessageType models types 1 through 7 and aliases type 8 to Other; no type 9, negotiation capability, replay buffer, Ack, Sequence, duplicate suppression, or backpressure exists. The repository has no GitHub Actions workflows and measured rustfmt/Clippy/warning debt prevents strict gates.

decisions.title: One lifecycle contract with target-specific runtime adapters
decisions.decision: Introduce one crate-internal ReconnectCoordinator that owns transitions, single-flight generation, policy attempts, cancellation, and recovery mode. Native and WASM adapters retain their existing synchronization models and provide connect, resume, send, close, and delay operations without reimplementing lifecycle policy. ReconnectionHandler exposes the existing reconnect, reconnect_with_policy, is_connected, and endpoint methods on both targets.
decisions.rationale: The current native and WASM state machines already diverge; sharing target locks is unsafe, while sharing only policy and transition ownership prevents semantic drift and preserves platform-idiomatic execution.

decisions.title: Fresh logical reconnect and stateful transport resume are distinct flows
decisions.decision: Persist an immutable internal ConnectionRecipe. A fresh reconnect calls HttpClient::negotiate with current authentication and protocol, obtains a new token, opens the socket, performs one JSON handshake, retains callbacks, and fails old pending calls without replay. A stateful resume reopens WebSockets at the current negotiated URL/token, sends no handshake, preserves pending calls, and invokes StatefulMessageBuffer resend.
decisions.rationale: Reusing an old token plus another handshake conflates a new logical connection with transport continuation. Explicit flows prevent unsafe application replay and match ASP.NET Core stateful behavior.

decisions.title: Official Ack/Sequence codec and bounded message buffer
decisions.decision: Add Ack=8 and Sequence=9 as distinct MessageType variants, exact JSON and MessagePack codecs, and one shared StatefulMessageBuffer over already serialized frames. The buffer sequences only types 1 through 5, uses u64 checked increments, records byte size, applies asynchronous backpressure at the configured threshold, sends delayed cumulative Ack messages, requires Sequence first after reconnect, validates resets, suppresses duplicates, and resends a stable snapshot after its own Sequence frame.
decisions.rationale: The protocol behavior is encoding-independent and must not be duplicated in transport loops. Buffering serialized frames preserves exact wire representation and avoids reserialization changes during replay.

evidence.reason: Normative message numbers and encodings.
Reference behavior for message classification, Ack timing, replay, backpressure, and duplicate handling.

alternativesRejected.alternative: Keep an unbounded Vec of frames
alternativesRejected.reason: A disconnected peer can cause unbounded memory growth and gives callers no backpressure.

alternativesRejected.alternative: Treat MessageType 8 as the existing Other variant
alternativesRejected.reason: Ack would be discarded and type 9 would remain unparseable.

After transport reconnect, client sends Sequence at first unacknowledged ID or total+1, resends snapshot, then permits new sends.
Incoming Sequence validates it is not ahead, resets next incoming ID, and subsequent duplicate trackable frames are discarded before application dispatch.
Incoming trackable traffic schedules one cumulative Ack after a one-second coalescing interval.

decisions.title: Deterministic checked-in interop harness
decisions.decision: Build a dedicated browser-facing WASM fixture, serve it locally, and drive real Chromium through a repository-local Playwright package modeled on RayX.GameX; expose bounded diagnostic state to Playwright, use Playwright-controlled network interruption for browser transport loss, add a native cfg(test)-only physical socket-drop hook, map ordinary and AllowStatefulReconnects=true endpoints in SignalRTestService, add deterministic synthetic ordered callback/stream scenarios, and provide one PowerShell 7 runner that validates selectors, builds/starts/health-checks the service, invokes the exact Playwright or Cargo scenario, enforces a 60-second scenario timeout, captures redacted diagnostics, and cleans up in finally semantics.
decisions.rationale: A real server and browser are required for SignalR transport proof. The established RayX.GameX pattern gives Playwright ownership of Chromium startup, shutdown, timeouts, traces, and assertions while the WASM fixture owns only protocol behavior and diagnostic publication; no WebDriver binary or Rust browser runner is needed.

decisions.title: Debt cleanup precedes immutable production gates
decisions.decision: After reconnect behavior is checkpointed, apply repository-wide rustfmt and resolve every compiler, Clippy, and rustdoc warning without broad allow attributes. Declare rust-version 1.92 and rust-toolchain.toml with rustfmt, clippy, and wasm target. Add quality.yml and interop.yml for pull_request, master push, and manual interop dispatch; use identical checked-in commands, contents-read permissions, concurrency cancellation, .NET 10, Chromium, RustSec and NuGet transitive scans, bounded timeouts, and failure-only artifacts.
decisions.rationale: Turning strict gates on before inherited debt is removed would create permanently red CI; postponing CI until after behavior proof avoids mixing mechanical global rewrites into reconnect checkpoints while still ending with enforced closure.
